Hi Sarah,

I have received the shipment. DHL delivered it quickly here to (address hidden).
The Bitfortun BS-4 miner is running well, and I have updated it with the
latest HARLO OS driver.

Everything looks good so far. Thank you for your prompt responses and for
keeping me updated. I appreciate your help.

Best regards,
Suman

Hi Suman,

Glad the BS-4 reached you in (address hidden) so quickly, and thanks for the photo. Your miner looks healthy. The screen shows 17.8 TH/s, ASIC at 49.4°C, the voltage regulator at 71.1°C and 326.6 W. That works out to roughly 18.3 J/TH, and both temperatures are comfortable. Your best share so far is 948.52M, and the miner's address on your network is 192.168.0.109.

The hashrate on that little screen is a live reading, so it will move up and down a bit. Your pool's figure is averaged over a longer window, so don't worry if the two don't match exactly.

About your firmware: we're not developing Harlo OS any further for now. You can keep running the build you have. If you ever have a firmware problem, the fix is to go back to the BS-4's stock firmware. For tips and settings, the community and our hardware lead JD (@nullhashrate) are very active on our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf

If you decide to push past the factory settings, a quick note: overclocking is at your own risk. If excess voltage, frequency or heat causes damage, the warranty may not cover it, so keep an eye on the ASIC and VR temperatures whenever you change anything.

Happy mining!

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Hi Hal and Team,

Sorry for the late reply and thank you for analyzing the details.

I waited a few days to see how performance held up, and it has been mining
consistently between 17.7 and 18.1 TH/s. However, the VR temperature
fluctuates between 69°C and 73°C (156°F to 162°F), which concerns me even
while running at the default 650 MHz and 1150 mV. This leaves no headroom
for overclocking.

To help lower the VR temperatures, I am thinking of installing two thin
fans (such as 80mm x 15mm) connected to the radiator fan ports using a
Noctua splitter. This will push air so the cap····and other chips stay
cooler. Any suggestions on fan size or the best way to set this up would be
highly appreciated.

As for Harlo OS, it has been very steady so far with minimal hashrate
fluctuation. I will keep your note in mind regarding reverting to the stock
Bitfortun firmware if any issues arise.

Thank you,
Suman

Hi Suman,

Thanks for the update. Holding 17.7 to 18.1 TH/s at default settings is right where a BS-4 should be.

I opened your new photo. It's a close-up of the board edge with a few small components, the white braided tubing and the cable bundle, all under the purple lighting. It's out of focus and I can't make out the regulators, so I can't judge anything thermal from it.

On the VR temperature: 69 to 73°C isn't dangerous. Bitfortun hasn't published the BS-4's own thermal limits. For reference, the open source ESP-Miner firmware that most of these boards build on
sets its throttle point at 105°C and its maximum at 145°C
 for this type of regulator. You have a good margin.

Your reading is higher than the factory figure, though. Our product page says the regulators
sit on the back of the board, in the path of the fan
, and quotes
53 degrees back there
 as measured at the factory. That's a lab number, and (address hidden) room temperature, the shelf and the firmware's sensor reading can all add to it. Still, more air across the back of the board is a sensible fix.

Your fan plan should work, with one change. I'd avoid running a splitter off the board's fan headers. We don't know how much current those headers can take. A second fan on the same header can also confuse the speed reading the firmware uses for fan control. Power the extra fans on their own instead, either 5V USB fans or 12V fans with their own plug-in adapter. Please don't wire anything into the Mean Well's screw terminals, because the mains input terminals sit right next to them.

For the setup itself:

1. A pair of 80 x 15 mm fans is a good size.
2. Point them at the back of the board, where the regulators are, and blow the same way as the radiator fan so the two don't push against each other.
3. Fix them to the stand or the shelf with zip ····printed bracket, not glue or tape on the board. That keeps it a clean add-on you can remove at any time.

Your setup is also boxed in by the wire shelf with the PSU right in front. A few centimetres of open space around the radiator exhaust often helps on its own.

On overclocking: going past the factory settings is at your own risk. The warranty may not cover damage from too much voltage, frequency or heat. If you do try it, watch both the ASIC and VR temperatures.

If you'd like to compare notes with other owners who have tried similar fan setups, the Discord is very active and JD is there as @nullhashrate: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
